scenario.summary: Storm-3119 (YAM Store) functions as an infrastructure broker that hijacks Microsoft 365 and Azure environments through automated reconnaissance and application-level credential abuse. These compromised environments and PaaS phishing kits (Storm-2990) are then used by downstream actors to conduct large-scale credential and financial theft, leveraging real-time victim interaction via WebSockets and Telegram.

meta.rationale: Focus on tenants with education (.edu) or non-profit (.org) identifiers, as these are specifically marketed in the YAM Store ecosystem. Look for activity originating from known proxy exit nodes.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary uses stolen application secrets for application-only authentication to hijack M365 tenants, subsequently escalating privileges via the Graph API to host phishing infrastructure on SharePoint and OneDrive.

hunt.name: Cloud Tenant Hijacking and Service Principal Abuse
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the lifecycle of cloud tenant hijacking as observed in the Storm-3119 ecosystem. It begins by identifying anomalous application-level authentication flows and sign-ins from proxy infrastructure (T1090.003). It then follows the chain to find privilege escalation through the self-provisioning of the PnP Management Shell and the abuse of sensitive directory permissions like AppCatalog.ReadWrite.All (T1098.003). By correlating initial access with follow-on resource manipulation, the hunt distinguishes between routine automation and the systematic hijacking of organizational storage for global phishing operations.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT cloud_account_uid, api_service_name FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find the M365 tenant IDs currently active in the API logs to narrow the investigation.
config.expected_signal: A list of cloud account UIDs representing active tenants. Silence suggests no M365 activity.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, api_operation, MIN(time) AS first_seen, COUNT(DISTINCT cloud_account_uid) AS tenant_count, COUNT(*) AS total_ops FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND (LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%resetpassword%' OR LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%assignlicense%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, api_operation HAVING tenant_count <= 1 ORDER BY total_ops DESC
config.description: Identify high-volume manipulation of accounts and licenses by service principals that are new to the environment.
config.expected_signal: A service principal performing password resets or license assignments that is new or rare in the environment.
